why_this_file_exists: ops.enforcement_control_catalog needs an enforcement_class per control, and rule-enforcement-map.json does not carry one. It is NOT added there because audits/guidance-situation-curation-review.v1.json pins that file by sha256 as the base inventory of a curation review that is still in review_state 'proposed'. Editing the map would invalidate a pending human review, and updating the recorded digest to match would assert a review that never happened. So the class lives here, beside the map rather than inside it, until that review is settled and the two can merge.
enforcement_class_is_a_property_of_the_c: Deriving the class from the rules that cite a control was tried first and rejected: deal_guard and loop_guard both fail as 'transaction refusal' yet their rules were tagged differently, because a rule's enforcement_class describes what the RULE does while this describes how the CONTROL fires.

controls_absent_from_the_map._note: Live in ops.enforcement_control_catalog since migration 0194 and declared in no inventory until the parity gate caught them on its first run. Declared here so the catalog has one complete source; fold them into the map when the pending curation review is settled.

human_authority_runtime.failure_mode: transaction refusal — an authority-only verb reached by a non-authority runtime is refused at the boundary

ci_gates.failure_mode: CI class failure — the gates class surfaces an enforcement-layer regression on every proposed change
ci_gates._note: Reconciled 2026-08-22: Production and staging carried implementation_ref 'ops/ci.sh gates class', prose naming a class inside a file rather than a path, so the reference could not resolve or be verified as tracked. Both databases now carry 'ops/ci.sh'; the class is named in test_ref and in the enforcement map already. The control was not locked by any active approved rule.

control-plane-workflow-manifest.failure_mode: Admission refusal — the manifest is the declared set of control-plane workflows, each naming a deterministic entrypoint and mode. A workflow that is not in it, or one that would reach for a model where the manifest declares a tested predicate, is refused rather than surfaced.
control-plane-workflow-manifest._note: Declared 2026-08-22 after ops/control-catalog-parity-gate.py reported it live in Production and present in no inventory — the second control to be found this way, after ci_gates. Unlike that one, nothing needed reconciling: Production's row already carries both refs as real tracked paths, so this declaration matches the live row exactly (implementation_ref ops/config/control-plane-workflows.v1.json, test_ref ops/control-plane-selftest.py, class deny_gate, installed true, verified 2026-08-16). Seeded by migration 0148 alongside the active rule it backs, the one forbidding a cognition token to be spent on state, recurrence, routing, validation or any decision already expressible as a tested predicate. That rule is the code-first design test in force, and this control is how it is enforced rather than recited.
